operations.title: Research state for the integrality gap of the CKR relaxation for Multiway Cut
operations.summary: The exact value of the global CKR integrality gap Γ remains unresolved, with current unconditional bounds 1.20016 ≤ Γ ≤ 1.2787. The Freund–Karloff midpoint family is represented as one durable research program. Its exact ratios yield Γ_k ≥ 8(k−1)/(7k−6), Γ ≥ 8/7, and a four-terminal ratio 12/11, but do not improve the global bracket or provide a universal upper bound.

operations.title: Exact integrality gap of the CKR relaxation
operations.summary: Determine the exact value of Γ = sup_{k≥3} Γ_k for conventional finite Multiway Cut instances. The question remains open. A frontier advance requires either an explicit certified lower bound above 1.20016 or a universal upper bound below 1.2787. The certified Freund–Karloff midpoint-family limit 8/7 and its lack of a universal rounding argument do not resolve the question.

operations.title: Current unconditional bounds on the CKR integrality gap
operations.summary: The current unconditional bounds are 1.20016 ≤ Γ ≤ 1.2787. The lower endpoint comes from an auxiliary non-opposite-cut problem on Δ₄ transferred to conventional instances with growing terminal count, not from a four-terminal CKR gap. The upper endpoint comes from an interval-certified rounding scheme. The midpoint family is compatible with but does not strengthen either endpoint: 12/11 and 8/7 are below 1.20016, and no improved universal upper bound is supplied.

operations.title: Freund–Karloff midpoint-family exact baseline
operations.summary: This program organizes the rational Freund–Karloff midpoint graph family H_k, its exact CKR and integral optima, the local finite cut lemma, the explicit H₄ certificate, and the resulting exact integrality ratios. For every k≥3, CKR(H_k)=(7k−6)/(8(k−1)) and OPT(H_k)=1, so the ratio tends to 8/7. The program is an exact baseline and regression resource rather than a frontier improvement. The family and ratio formula are attributed to Ari Freund and Howard Karloff; the supporting transaction contributes reconstruction and verification work.

operations.title: Rational midpoint graph family H_k
operations.summary: For each integer k≥3, H_k has terminals t₁,…,t_k and a midpoint m_{ij} for every terminal pair. Each terminal–midpoint outer edge has weight a=1/(k−1)². For every terminal triple, its three midpoint vertices form a triangle whose edges have weight b=3/(2k(k−1)²). The family has k+binom(k,2) vertices, k(k−1) outer edges, and 3binom(k,3) inner edges. The rational weights, normalization, symbolic family, H₄ specialization, and verifier are mutually consistent.

operations.title: Exact CKR value of the midpoint family
operations.summary: For every integer k≥3, CKR(H_k)=(7k−6)/(8(k−1)). The optimal embedding sends each terminal t_i to e_i and each midpoint m_{ij} to (e_i+e_j)/2. Every edge then has half-ℓ₁ length 1/2. A matching convex subgradient certificate gives the constant midpoint subgradient μ·1, where μ=3(k−2)/(4k(k−1)²), proving global optimality even though midpoint vectors lie on the simplex boundary. The exact verifier checks the corresponding rational stationarity calculation for k=4; the all-k theorem rests on the symbolic argument.

operations.title: Exact integral optimum of the midpoint family
operations.summary: For every integer k≥3, OPT(H_k)=1. For an integral labeling, if q counts midpoints assigned outside their endpoint pair, the averaged local weighting W satisfies C_W≥1−q/(3binom(k,3)), while the outer-edge weighting W′ satisfies C_W′=1+q/binom(k,2). In the convex combination ((k−2)/(k−1))W+(1/(k−1))W′, the q terms cancel and the resulting weights equal those of H_k, proving a lower bound of 1. Assigning m_{ij} label i for i<j attains cost 1.

operations.title: Three-midpoint local cut bounds
operations.summary: For three selected terminals and their three pair-midpoint vertices, give each of the six terminal–midpoint edges weight 1/6 and each midpoint-triangle edge weight 1/4. Every assignment of the three midpoints from four labels has cut cost at least 2/3, and every non-opposite assignment has cost at least 1. Exact enumeration covers all 4³=64 assignments. In the global averaging argument, a midpoint labeled outside its endpoint pair can cause at most one selected terminal triple to violate the non-opposite condition.

operations.title: Four-terminal midpoint instance H_4
operations.summary: The k=4 specialization has 4 terminals, 6 midpoint nonterminals, 10 vertices, 12 outer edges of weight 1/9, 12 inner edges of weight 1/24, and 24 edges total. Its exact values are CKR(H₄)=11/12 and OPT(H₄)=1, giving ratio 12/11. An exact-arithmetic verifier exhausts all 4⁶=4096 assignments and finds 28 minimizers. This finite instance does not establish a four-terminal ratio of 1.20016.

operations.title: Integrality ratios furnished by the midpoint family
operations.summary: For every k≥3, OPT(H_k)/CKR(H_k)=8(k−1)/(7k−6)=8/(7+1/(k−1)). Consequently Γ_k≥8(k−1)/(7k−6), and taking k→∞ gives Γ≥8/7. The four-terminal specialization gives Γ₄≥12/11. These are exact classical baseline bounds, but 8/7<1.20016, and the family supplies no universal upper bound. The four-label local lemma does not turn the limiting 8/7 result into a four-terminal CKR gap.
